findings.title: Group canManage() treats VIEW as manage
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) succeeds, so a caller who only has the Groups VIEW scope is treated as allowed to manage every group. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() (and any other requireManage() caller) therefore lets a view-only fine-grained admin create groups. V1 canManage() only checks MANAGE_USERS, and canManage(GroupModel) correctly checks only MANAGE. The VIEW scope must not satisfy canManage(); the interface comment that lists VIEW looks copied from canView().

findings.title: View-members group filter uses authz resource ids
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() walks resources with findByType and then calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). V2 group resources are stored under the group id as the resource name (resolveGroup returns group.getId()), while getId() is the authorization resource UUID. hasPermission looks that value up with findByName, so the per-group permission check misses and falls back to the all-groups resource. The set passed to UserModel.GROUPS / getUsersCount is therefore not a set of group ids. User search and user counts for admins who can only view members of specific groups (UsersResource, BruteForceUsersResource) will drop those users or match the wrong groups.

findings.title: Created group resources never get type Groups
findings.body: getOrCreateResource() creates a resource and updates scopes but never calls resource.setType(resourceType). V1 group resources were typed "Group". GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() only discovers groups via resourceStore.findByType(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE). Without the type, individual group permission resources are invisible to that scan, so membership-based user visibility cannot be computed even after the id/name mix-up is fixed. The all-groups resource created in init() does set the type; per-object resources must do the same.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not upgraded for Groups
findings.body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already non-null, and that is the only place scopes and the "Groups" resource type are created. Realms that already enabled FGAP V2 (client created with only Users/Clients) never receive GROUPS, manage-membership, manage-members, or view-members. Creating a group permission then fails in getOrCreateResource with ModelException "No scopes found", and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() NPEs when getResourceTypeResource() returns null and that null is passed to policyStore.findByResource / resource.getScopes(). Schema init needs an idempotent update path for new resource types and scopes.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong check
findings.body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) is false. The implementation throws when canManageMembers is false. Callers reading only the interface will enforce or test the wrong scope (manage-membership vs manage-members).
